key_insight: Quantum Spectral Models encode each matrix input through an input-conditioned Hamiltonian, so the model’s spectral values and subspaces directly shape its learned Fourier features.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum machine learning a more structure-aware inductive bias for matrix data, with a path toward interpretable, task-matched circuit design.
method: Build the data-encoding unitary generator directly from the input matrix.
Use three Hamiltonian variants: symmetric, global block, and non-overlapping patch-local blocks.
Exploit truncated Fourier representations where spectral gaps act as phase carriers and spectral subspaces determine coefficients.
evidence_signal: Across four benchmarks, the QSM variants achieved the best mean test accuracy at the largest circuit depth, with patch-local QSM best on Pendigits and global block-Hamiltonian QSM best on the synthetic spectral tasks.
watch_item: Performance depends on task structure and circuit depth, so the spectral inductive bias may not transfer uniformly and adds Hamiltonian-construction overhead.
paper_title: Quantum Spectral Model: Data Reuploading with Input-Conditioned Frequency Support
